_metadata.description: 15 additional Aggregation-Operator (AO) pairs, constructed for the peer-review revision to broaden the AO category's domain diversity beyond the original 10 TPC-H-flavored pairs (data/conflict_dataset_ao_10.json). Combined with the original 10, this gives a 25-pair AO-25 set (data/conflict_dataset_ao_25.json is the two files concatenated by experiments/run_a6_ao25_eval.py at load time). Each pair still holds tables, columns, and filter-logic operator topology fixed across both sides and varies only the aggregation function (or, for one pair, aggregation plus topology together, mirroring the original set's one double-conflict pair), so D3 and D4 cannot distinguish either side of any pair by construction.
_metadata.labeling_methodology: Single-pass, single-labeler (same author as the original 10-pair AO set), same construction discipline: every pair's ground-truth label was fixed at construction time, not assigned after the fact to an ambiguous real pair. IMPORTANT, and disclosed here rather than only in the paper's Limitations: these 15 pairs are, like the original 10, constructed examples spanning a deliberately wider set of business domains (SaaS, HR, logistics, ad-tech, retail, finance, education, energy, manufacturing, telecom, gaming) to reduce over-fitting to one schema family -- they are NOT sourced from real enterprise metric definitions or any production semantic layer. No second labeler or inter-rater agreement statistic exists for this dataset either. Sourcing real (even anonymized) enterprise metric-definition pairs was identified as a follow-up during peer review and is named explicitly as unresolved future work, not silently addressed by broadening domains alone.
_metadata.created_for: extension_paper peer-review revision, Group A3 extension (broadening AO domain diversity)

pairs.name: mrr: SUM vs COUNT over identical scope (SaaS)
pairs.rationale: Monthly recurring revenue (SUM of mrr_amount) and active-subscription count (COUNT) are different SaaS KPIs that happen to share the exact same lineage and filter.

pairs.name: headcount: COUNT vs SUM(fte_fraction) over identical scope (HR)
pairs.rationale: Headcount (COUNT of employees) and full-time-equivalent headcount (SUM of fte_fraction) diverge whenever any employee is part-time, despite identical lineage.

pairs.name: shipment_weight: SUM vs AVG over identical scope (logistics)
pairs.rationale: Total shipped weight (SUM) and average shipment weight (AVG) are distinct logistics metrics over an identical join and filter.

pairs.name: campaign_spend_total: SUM vs MAX over identical scope (ad-tech)
pairs.rationale: Total campaign spend (SUM) and the single largest spend event (MAX) are not interchangeable, despite an identical lineage and channel filter.

pairs.name: basket_value: AVG vs SUM over identical scope (retail)
pairs.rationale: Average basket value (AVG) and total online revenue (SUM) are different retail metrics over the same order/order_items join and channel filter.

pairs.name: approved_expense: SUM vs MIN over identical scope (finance)
pairs.rationale: Total approved expense (SUM) and the smallest single approved expense (MIN) are unrelated quantities that share a lineage and status filter.

pairs.name: attendance: COUNT vs SUM(days_present) over identical scope (education)
pairs.rationale: Number of attendance records (COUNT) and total days present (SUM of days_present) diverge whenever a record can represent more than one day.

pairs.name: energy_usage: SUM vs AVG over identical scope (energy/utilities)
pairs.rationale: Total energy consumption (SUM) and average per-reading consumption (AVG) are distinct utility metrics over an identical meter/reading join and filter.

pairs.name: defect_count: COUNT vs SUM(defect_qty) over identical scope (manufacturing)
pairs.rationale: Number of defect events (COUNT) and total defective units (SUM of defect_qty) diverge whenever an event can report more than one unit.

pairs.name: call_duration: SUM vs AVG over identical scope (telecom)
pairs.rationale: Total outbound call minutes (SUM) and average outbound call duration (AVG) are different telecom KPIs over an identical lineage and filter.

pairs.name: session_length: AVG vs SUM over identical scope (gaming)
pairs.rationale: Average session length (AVG) and total playtime (SUM) are distinct engagement metrics over the same player/session join and platform filter.

pairs.name: conversions: COUNT vs SUM(conversion_value) plus AND-to-OR filter change (double conflict, marketing)
pairs.rationale: Two independent conflict signals at once (AND-to-OR filter-topology change and a different aggregation function) -- D4 alone already flags this via the topology diff; D5 must continue to flag it too, mirroring the original AO set's one double-conflict pair.

pairs.name: conversions_count: COUNT vs COUNT identical (negative control, marketing)
pairs.rationale: Negative control: tables, columns, filter logic, and aggregation function are all identical -- must not be flagged.

pairs.name: churn_mrr: sum vs SUM case-normalization (negative control, SaaS)
pairs.rationale: Negative control for aggregation_fn normalization: "sum" and "SUM" must normalize to the same canonical value and not be flagged.

pairs.name: shipment_count: SUM vs SUM, threshold-only variant (negative control, logistics)
pairs.rationale: Both sides sum the same column over the same join path; only the weight threshold changed (same shape as the original dataset's TV category). A matching aggregation_fn with a threshold-only filter change must not be flagged.
